Enumerate numbers of individual profiles and group classes

Source: R/enumeration.R
enumerate_classes.Rd

Fits every requested combination of profile count, group-class count and covariance structure and returns the candidates with their information criteria and classification diagnostics. Errors and warnings of each candidate are kept in the table alongside the successful fits. Information criteria are descriptive: neither the smallest BIC nor high entropy guarantees the correct number of classes. Unconverged, boundary and unreplicated fits are reported, not silently selected.

Usage

enumerate_classes(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles = 1:4,
  n_group_classes = 1:3,
  model = "basic",
  seed = NULL,
  family = "profiles",
  between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  time = NULL,
  ...,
  cores = 1L,
  type = NULL,
  verbose = cores > 1L
)

Arguments

data

Data frame.

vars

Indicator column names.

id

The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in (students in schools, reports in students). Required; NULL enumerates single-level models, with a message. enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_lca() fit single-level models directly.

n_profiles

Positive integer profile counts to try. Default 1:4.

n_group_classes

Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default 1:3. With id = NULL it is 1 and may be left out.

model

The covariance structures to cross with the class counts. "basic" (the default) fits four structures: "EEI" (equal variances, no covariances), "VVI" (varying variances, no covariances), "EEE" (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and "VVV" (a covariance matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated indicators tends to favour additional profiles. "all" fits all 14 structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by their three-letter codes, as multilpa()'s model takes them: the letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's covariance matrix, each equal (E) or varying (V) across profiles, with I for no covariances. NULL crosses no structures. With one continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance) are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is crossed. A structure set through variance_model, covariance_model, volume, shape or orientation in ... replaces the default.

seed

Optional seed for each fit: a whole number set.seed() accepts. Anything else raises latents_bad_argument before any candidate is fitted.

family

"profiles" (the default) enumerates the profile model over n_profiles, n_group_classes and model. One or more of the group-class families "additive", "dispersion" and "additive_dispersion" enumerates those instead, over family, n_group_classes and between_variance; these need id, n_profiles and model are then refused, and the result is a latents_family_enumeration, read with get_results() and get_candidate().

between_variance

For group-class families: the between-variance restrictions to cross, "varying", "equal" or both (the default). The dispersion family is always fitted with "equal". Refused for the profile family.

time

The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models (lta()) over n_profiles (default 2:4) and n_group_classes (default 1), with every other lta() argument given in ... held fixed. model, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only the profile family is available. The result is a latents_transition_enumeration, read with get_results() and get_candidate().

...

Further arguments to multilpa() (or to lta() with time), applied to every candidate, such as n_starts (random starts per candidate), max_iter, missing, categorical, centering, scaling, drop_empty and boundary ("exclude" sets aside starts with a variance at min_variance, degenerate solutions that become more likely as n_starts grows). For example, enumerate_classes(data, vars, id, n_profiles = 2:6, n_starts = 20, seed = 1). Group-class families take only n_starts, max_iter, tol and min_variance.

cores

Number of processor cores to fit the candidates on (default 1). Each candidate sets and restores its own random seed, so with seed given the result is identical to cores = 1. Candidates are fitted by forked processes on macOS and Linux, and by a socket cluster on Windows and on macOS when R uses Apple's Accelerate BLAS (socket workers load the installed package). Warnings and messages from the workers are passed on in grid order once all have finished. Without seed, the random starts differ between runs on any number of cores. Lost worker results are retried once with half as many workers (rounded up). One latents_worker_lost warning reports how many tasks were lost and recovered, and suggests fewer cores. A task still lost becomes a failed start (for flat start grids) or a failed candidate; the other results are retained. On sockets, bounded chunks preserve earlier results when a connection breaks; completed tasks within the failed chunk may also be retried. Each core holds its own copy of the fits it computes; parallel::detectCores() gives the number available. Transition grids (time) and profile grids (including categorical-only latent class models) distribute individual starts across one pool, longest estimated first, with at most cores workers and no nested workers. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool; search keeps the same defaults as multilpa(). Setup, ordered starting values, start selection and finalisation stay in the current process. Profile models with membership covariates or joined categorical local_dependence pairs instead occupy one worker per candidate in the same pool, with serial starts. Group-class families also keep candidate-level parallelism.

type

Optional model type: "lca", "lpa" or "lta". NULL (the default) keeps the existing routing and measurement settings. "lca" treats every indicator as categorical, as multilca() does: indicators named in ordinal or count keep those distributions, and categorical adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response codes are categorical with type = "lca". "lpa" requires continuous indicators and refuses non-empty categorical, ordinal or count. Both require time = NULL. "lta" requires time and takes its measurement settings from categorical, as lta() does; it does not make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires family = "profiles"; leave type = NULL for group-class families.

verbose

Whether to report progress: one message each when the candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when cores > 1, where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (family) are not reported.

Value

An object of class multilpa_enumeration (or the transition or family enumeration described above). Its type records the resolved model: "lca", "lpa" or "lta", or "mixed"/"family" for those grids under type = NULL. The print header shows this type; table columns are unchanged. as.data.frame() gives one row per candidate, starting with its name ("profiles3_groups2"), with every criterion and diagnostic (including both entropies and, at each level, the smallest, largest and mean average posterior probability and the number of classes below a cutoff) and the candidate's warnings and error. get_results(x, "best") names the candidate at each criterion's minimum; get_results(x, "classification") gives every class's average posterior probability and relative entropy for every candidate; get_results(x, "deltas") and "knees" give model-selection evidence. summary() prints each criterion's minimum and every table, plot() draws the information criteria (and, with what, classification quality and model-selection views), get_candidate() returns the fitted model of one candidate, and compare_models() puts candidates side by side; these verbs take candidates by name.

Conditions

latents_bad_argument when model names an unknown structure, when it is given together with another way of setting the structure, or when it is given although no indicator is continuous; when seed is not a seed set.seed() accepts; when ... contains an argument multilpa() does not take; when n_group_classes other than 1 is given with id = NULL; when id is missing; when between_variance is given for the profile family; when n_profiles or model is given for a group-class family, or id is NULL; when time is combined with a group-class family or with between_variance; and when cores is not a whole number of at least 1; and when type is invalid or conflicts with time, family or the requested measurement distributions.

References

Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models. Pattern Recognition, 28(5), 781–793.

See also

get_candidate() to take one fitted model out of the grid, summary() for the criterion-by-criterion comparison.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100))
candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,
                              n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
as.data.frame(candidates)

# Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical:
codes <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10), item = rep(0:1, 50))
classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",
                             n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,
                             n_starts = 1, seed = 1)

# Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures:
single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",
                                "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),
                        n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),
                        n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
summary(single)
